https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/c4gw16.text: 'Incredible': SpaceX rocket spotted off Christmas Island coast 'Incredible': SpaceX rocket spotted off Christmas Island coast Close A SpaceX rocket has made an unexpected appearance off Christmas Island after touching down in the Indian Ocean following a test flight from Texas on 24 July. David Watchorn, chair of the Christmas Island Tourism Association said he initially thought he was looking at ships on his way to work, before realising it was "a rocket, a space rocket" being towed. The 52-metre long rocket has caused a stir among locals, with some "sneaking out" of work for a glimpse, and others preparing their boats for a closer look at the debris. "It's really incredible to think about what it's been through," Watchorn told the BBC. "The more and more you look at it, the more fascinating it's becoming". https://www.politico.eu/article/ed-milib.text: LONDON — U.K. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is to attend a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Ireland as he pushes for closer ties with Europe. The attendance by Britain’s top diplomat at the summit, which runs Tuesday and Wednesday, is the latest sign that Miliband wants to prioritize relations with Britain’s European neighbors. The Foreign Office said last month that Miliband would play a leading role in relations with the EU — an exercise which in previous administrations has been run out of Downing Street or overseen by separate departments. Advertisement Advertisement “Working closely with our European neighbours will make Britain a wealthier, safer country- that is why I am putting the European relationship at the heart of my agenda as Foreign Secretary,” Miliband said ahead of the meeting, which will take place in Wicklow in Ireland. The foreign secretary is set to hold a series of bilateral meetings, including with his EU counterpart Kaja Kallas and German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul. He is also due to meet his Irish counterpart Helen McEntree, Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand and Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha — the latter two also attending the meeting as guests. Ahead of the meeting the Foreign Office said the discussions would focus on deepening U.K. cooperation with European and international partners, as well as supporting Ukraine. He is expected to announce new British funding to support reconstruction in the invasion-hit country, as well as measures to allow British companies to participate in rebuilding efforts there. Ministers will also discuss wider challenges facing the continent such as climate pressures — following the hottest summer on record in the U.K. The so-called “Gymnich” meeting is meant to be a more informal setting than most EU summits so leaders can speak candidly without officials. The format is named after the German castle Schloss Gymnich which hosted the first such meeting in 1974. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.politico.eu/article/even-tru.text: BRUSSELS — The EU's plans for a deeper partnership with Canada, aimed at helping the country withstand a trade war with the U.S., have won the support of governments across the political spectrum — including those usually cautious about angering Donald Trump's administration. Ambassadors representing the bloc's 27 governments met in Brussels on Wednesday to discuss the move, just hours after the White House banned Canadian exports of dairy, alcohol and motorbikes in an escalating tariff feud. The EU's idea would see ties strengthened in areas like technology, trade and critical raw materials, according to two people in the meeting who were granted anonymity by POLITICO because the talks were confidential. Despite the risk of the EU being seen to side against Washington, no capital raised objections, they said. The European Commission and the European Council jointly presented preparations for a landmark summit with Canada on Oct. 29-30, committing to explore new areas where they will step up their partnership. That includes sectors like technology, research and innovation, as well as mining for valuable rare metals and breaking down trade barriers, those involved said. Advertisement Advertisement "There’s very strong support for [Commission President] von der Leyen making that outreach and for closer cooperation," said a third diplomat with knowledge of the preparations. That's despite a handful of countries, including Giorgia Meloni's Italy, Andrej Babiš's Czech Republic and Robert Fico's Slovakia, traditionally seeking close ties with the Trump camp and trying to avoid outright provocations. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will address the European Parliament next week on a trip first reported by POLITICO , as part of a public campaign to pivot away from dependency on the U.S. and form a club of like-minded, pro-free trade democracies. The visit is designed "to clearly signal the intention and ambition on both sides to upgrade our partnership," a senior EU official said. From the Arctic to the universities Carney's trip, which coincides with von der Leyen's State of the Union speech, has sparked a search for concrete ideas on areas for closer collaboration. Participation in the EU's Erasmus student exchange scheme, alignment on security and defense in the Arctic region and military-industrial partnerships are among those areas being considered, according to nine EU officials and one diplomat familiar with the discussions. No broad new partnership has been agreed, however, and officials cautioned that talks remain at an early stage. For now, the aim is to demonstrate political ambition and identify areas where the two sides can deepen cooperation, with Carney expected to set out more practical next steps in his speech. The Commission is preparing an updated Arctic policy, currently expected on Oct. 20 and renamed the North Neighbourhood and Arctic Strategy to reflect its broader geographic focus. Von der Leyen, meanwhile, recently returned from Greenland saying Europe wanted to become “more engaged in the Arctic.” That makes the region a potentially useful bridge between Brussels’ strategic priorities and Ottawa’s. Another EU official said any reference to Canada in the speech could center on security, potentially through some form of Arctic security initiative. “Security and defense is always her happy place,” the official said when asked what form an overture to Carney might take. Cooperation in the region could extend well beyond defense. A third official who has worked on the Arctic strategy pointed to existing and potential cooperation on critical raw materials, subsea cables and specialized equipment needed to operate in the High North, including icebreakers and other Arctic-capable vessels. Cleaner shipping is another area where the two sides’ interests overlap — and diverge from the U.S., which has lobbied against decarbonization in the industry . Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.techspot.com/news/114059-bil.text: Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years. TechSpot means tech analysis and advice you can trust . Forward-looking: Almost 10 years after he first raised the issue, Bill Gates has repeated his warning that robots should pay taxes. The Microsoft co-founder points out that as automation takes more people's jobs, the amount of tax being paid will fall. The solution, he believes, is to make robots pay the same FICA taxes that humans would. Speaking to Ezra Klein of The New York Times, Gates said that society should get to decide how to protect its workers even if it's making them jobless. The billionaire described a unit of labor that could be defined so that work done by either humans or robots would be subject to the same FICA tax. The US payroll tax funds Social Security and Medicare. Employees generally pay 7.65% of wages: 6.2% for Social Security and 1.45% for Medicare, with employers paying a matching amount. High earners can also owe an additional Medicare tax. Automation-related job losses on an apocalyptic scale could be disastrous for society. Not only would the government see a drastic decline in tax revenue, those laid off would struggle financially. Gates said taxing robots could provide economic security for citizens while allowing governments to keep collecting taxes. He says the money could come from the savings companies make from not having to employ human workers. "Just because the economic signals say that it'd be lower cost to use an AI doesn't mean society has to do that," he said. // Related Stories Bill Gates says tech executives are privately terrified of AI, but won't say it publicly Former CIA chief says AI could begin directing battlefield weapons by 2030 In August, Gates published a nearly 6,000-word essay titled The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical . He warned that the transition to the AI era will be one of the most turbulent times in human history. And that right now, we are not preparing adequately for that transition. That essay also called for robots to be taxed, along with AI tokens. "If you're an employer and you hire someone, you pay payroll taxes on their earnings," Gates wrote. "But if you buy a robot, you can usually write it off right away as a business expense. The tax system nudges you toward replacing people with machines." Gates also believes an AI tax would slow the rush away from human labor and raise money for retraining and a stronger safety net. AI continues to be responsible for thousands of job losses, either through direct replacements or indirectly as companies prioritize resources toward the technology – despite execs now trying to play down the scope of the impact. Jobloss.ai reports that there have been just under 130,000 AI-related job losses in the US since January 2025. It's not just white-collar jobs under threat. Companies are starting to eye robots for positions beyond warehouses and factories. One California county is taking the issue so seriously that it wants businesses to pay a fee when robots take someone's job, while a protest over the issue in Poland even included robots. Gates first called for a robot tax in 2017, years before ChatGPT arrived. Back then, he said the tax could also be used to help people who've lost their jobs to automation by funding training for positions that require human empathy and understanding, such as care for the elderly and children with special needs. 16 comments 288 likes and shares Share this article: See more TechSpot in Google Add us as a preferred source and our reporting shows up first when you search.
